p: not: We ought to find fault with one another, but we must beware we do not do it without cause, or to seem holier than others or because of hatred of others.
Give not that which is holy: The stiff-necked and stubborn enemies of the gospel are unworthy to have it preached unto them.

pearls before swine: A pearl is known among the Greeks for its oriental brightness: and a pearl was in ancient times greatly valued by the Latins: for a pearl that Cleopatra had was valued at two hundred and fifty thousand crowns: and the word is now borrowed from that, to signify the most precious heavenly doctrine.
Ask: Prayers are a sure refuge in all miseries.
Therefore all things whatsoever ye would: An explanation of the meaning of the second table.
law and the prophets: That is to say, The doctrine of the law and prophets.
Enter ye in at the strait: The example of life must not be taken from the multitude.
strait is the gate: The way is straight and narrow: we must pass through this rough way and suffer, endure, be changed and so enter into life.
Beware of false prophets: False teachers must be taken heed of: and they are known by false doctrine and evil living.
Not every one that saith unto: Even the best gifts that exist are nothing without godliness.
name: By "name" here is meant mighty working power of God, which every man witnesses that calls upon him.

wonderful works: Properly, powers: Now these excellent works which are done are called powers because of those things which they bring to pass, for by them we understand how mighty the power of God is.
I never knew you: This is not of ignorance, but because he will cast them away.
ye that work iniquity: You that are given to all kinds of wickedness, and seem to make an art of sin.
Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of: True godliness rests only upon Christ, and therefore always remains invincible.
